articles.title: Patient perspectives of participation in clinical studies in late-onset Pompe disease: Structured exit interviews from cipaglucosidase alfa plus miglustat studies
articles.summary: This study presents structured exit interview data from patients with late-onset Pompe disease who participated in clinical trials evaluating cipaglucosidase alfa combined with miglustat. The research captures patient perspectives and experiences during their involvement in these treatment studies. The findings provide qualitative insight into patient participation in rare disease clinical research.

articles.title: Mitigating the Devastation: A Parent's Perspective on Her Child's Exclusion From a Clinical Trial for a Rare Disease Drug Therapy
articles.summary: This qualitative perspective examines a parent's experience with their child's exclusion from a clinical trial for a rare disease treatment, highlighting a gap in academic literature that focuses heavily on disease natural history, trial design innovations, and therapeutic development while largely overlooking the patient and family perspectives on trial participation barriers.

articles.title: Comparative pharmacovigilance of glycaemic adverse-event reporting for alpelisib and capivasertib: A disproportionality analysis of the FDA adverse event monitoring system
articles.summary: This pharmacovigilance study compared glucose-related adverse event reporting patterns for two PI3K inhibitors, alpelisib and capivasertib, using disproportionality analysis of FDA adverse event data to identify potential safety signal differences between these agents.

articles.title: Risk of Clostridioides difficile infection with potassium-competitive acid blockers: A systematic review with restricted quantitative synthesis
articles.summary: This systematic review with restricted quantitative synthesis evaluates the risk of Clostridioides difficile infection associated with potassium-competitive acid blockers, a newer class of gastric acid suppressants. The analysis synthesizes available evidence to assess whether these medications carry a clinically meaningful infection risk compared to other acid-suppressive therapies. Findings from this review may inform clinical decision-making regarding the selection of acid-suppressive agents in patients at risk for C. difficile infection.

articles.title: Integrating Artificial Intelligence with High-Throughput Biological Testing for Antimicrobial Drug Discovery
articles.summary: This review examines the integration of artificial intelligence with high-throughput biological testing platforms to accelerate antimicrobial drug discovery. The approach combines machine learning algorithms with rapid screening methods to identify and optimize novel antimicrobial compounds more efficiently than traditional approaches. This integrated strategy addresses the growing challenge of antimicrobial resistance by enabling faster identification of promising drug candidates.

articles.title: Nanotherapeutic Strategies Targeting Senescent Microenvironment for Aging-Related Chronic Diseases
articles.summary: This review examines nanotherapeutic strategies designed to target the senescent microenvironment as a treatment approach for aging-related chronic diseases. Nanoparticle-based therapies are evaluated for their potential to address the cellular and tissue-level changes associated with cellular senescence in aging. The article presents current evidence on how nanotherapeutics may modulate senescent cell activity and improve outcomes in age-related disease management.

articles.title: Clinical inertia among patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus in upper-middle-income countries: A systematic review and meta-analysis
articles.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis examines clinical inertia—the failure to initiate or intensify therapy despite inadequate glycemic control—among patients with type 2 diabetes in upper-middle-income countries. The study synthesizes evidence on the prevalence and impact of delayed treatment intensification in this population and geographic setting. Findings address a significant gap in understanding barriers to optimal diabetes management in resource-limited healthcare systems.

articles.title: Improving timeliness of antihypertensive treatment intensification through pharmacist-led interventions among older adult patients in Northwest Ethiopia: Multicenter prospective cohort study
articles.summary: This multicenter prospective cohort study evaluated pharmacist-led interventions to improve the timeliness of antihypertensive treatment intensification in older adult patients across healthcare facilities in Northwest Ethiopia. The intervention model, delivered by clinical pharmacists, aimed to optimize blood pressure management by accelerating treatment adjustments when needed. Results demonstrate the effectiveness of pharmacist-led clinical services in enhancing the speed and appropriateness of hypertension management in this patient population.

articles.title: Comparative effectiveness and safety of leflunomide versus methotrexate in the treatment of elderly rheumatoid arthritis patients: A retrospective cohort study
articles.summary: This retrospective cohort study compared the effectiveness and safety of leflunomide versus methotrexate for treating rheumatoid arthritis in elderly patients. The analysis evaluated clinical outcomes and adverse event profiles between the two disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs in this older patient population.

articles.title: Animal and Cell Models in Alzheimer's and Parkinson's Disease: Current Innovations Reviewed
articles.summary: Alzheimer's disease and Parkinson's disease represent significant global health burdens with complex underlying pathology and no current curative treatments, creating a critical need for reliable experimental models. This review examines current innovations in animal and cell-based models used to advance understanding of these neurodegenerative diseases and support the development of new therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: Epileptiform Discharges in Seizure-Free Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder and the Role of Antiseizure Medications
articles.summary: This study investigates the frequency of epileptiform discharges—abnormal electrical brain activity patterns—in children with autism spectrum disorder who have not experienced clinical seizures, and examines the potential role of antiseizure medications in managing this condition.

articles.title: MENTOR: An Evidence-Informed Large Language Model-Based Multi-Agent System for Efficient Selection of Institution-Specific Negative Control Outcomes
articles.summary: Objective Negative control outcomes (NCOs) help detect and correct systematic error in observational studies, yet their selection remains largely manual. The Common Evidence Model (CEM) can generate candidate lists, but researchers must still screen them for plausibility as true nulls and for sufficient observation in each institution's data. articles.summary: This epidemiological study examined the prevalence, incidence, clinical presentation, and treatment patterns of polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) in UK primary care settings over a 27-year period from 1998 to 2025. The research was conducted by researchers at the Centre for Clinical Epidemiology at McGill University and affiliated institutions, utilizing primary care data to characterize disease burden and management approaches in a real-world setting.

articles.title: Accelerating Lead Optimization Away from Anti-Targets: Navigating the Structural Complexity of Promiscuous ADMET Proteins
articles.summary: This study addresses the structural complexity of promiscuous absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity (ADMET) proteins to accelerate lead optimization while minimizing off-target binding. The research presents computational and experimental approaches to navigate the binding selectivity challenges posed by these structurally complex proteins during drug discovery.

articles.title: Asparagus horridus spirostanol saponins and their antischistosomal and antinociceptive potential: evidence from in vivo and in silico research
articles.summary: Spirostanol saponins isolated from Asparagus horridus were evaluated for activity against schistosomiasis and pain using both animal studies and computer-based molecular modeling approaches. The research combined in vivo efficacy testing with in silico analysis to characterize the antischistosomal and antinociceptive potential of these natural compounds.

articles.title: Stimuli-responsive CRISPR-based genome editing delivery system for cancer treatment: A review of fundamentals and applications
articles.summary: This review examines stimuli-responsive delivery systems designed to transport CRISPR-based genome editing tools to cancer cells, covering the underlying principles and clinical applications of this emerging therapeutic approach. Stimuli-responsive systems are engineered to release their cargo in response to specific internal or external triggers, potentially improving the precision and efficacy of CRISPR-mediated cancer treatment. The article synthesizes current knowledge on how these targeted delivery mechanisms may enhance therapeutic outcomes while reducing off-target effects.

articles.title: 3β-trans-CLD alleviates metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) via modulating the IDO1/Nrf2/SREBP1/SCD1 axis in vitro
articles.summary: 3β-trans-CLD, a compound from traditional Chinese medicine sources, demonstrates therapeutic potential for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) through in vitro modulation of the IDO1/Nrf2/SREBP1/SCD1 signaling pathway. The study identifies a molecular mechanism by which 3β-trans-CLD may reduce hepatic lipid accumulation by targeting key regulators of lipid metabolism and oxidative stress.

articles.title: Safety of proton pump inhibitors in children: A systematic review
articles.summary: This systematic review evaluates the safety profile of proton pump inhibitors in the pediatric population. The analysis synthesizes evidence on adverse effects and safety considerations specific to children receiving this drug class. The findings aim to inform clinical practice and regulatory decision-making regarding proton pump inhibitor use in pediatric patients.

articles.title: GPCRAgent: an intelligent multi-agent platform integrating knowledge graphs and large language models for GPCR-targeted drug discovery
articles.summary: GPCRAgent is an intelligent multi-agent platform that combines knowledge graphs and large language models to support drug discovery targeting G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs). The platform integrates advanced computational approaches to enhance GPCR-targeted therapeutic development.

articles.title: Clinical Characteristics and Outcomes of Community-Onset and Hospital-Onset Sepsis Patients: The Korean Nationwide Sepsis Cohort Study
articles.summary: This Korean nationwide cohort study examines clinical characteristics and patient outcomes in sepsis cases occurring in community versus hospital settings. The research, conducted by the Korean Sepsis Alliance, involved investigators from multiple institutions including Asan Medical Center and Samsung Advanced Institute for Health Sciences, and provides comparative epidemiological data on sepsis presentation and outcomes across these two distinct onset populations.

articles.title: Next-Generation Cancer Nanovaccines: Reprogramming the Tumor Microenvironment from Rational Design Toward Clinical Translation
articles.summary: Next-generation cancer nanovaccines aim to reprogram the tumor microenvironment through rational design principles to enable clinical translation. This approach represents an advancement in cancer immunotherapy that leverages nanotechnology to modify the immune landscape within tumors. The review synthesizes current knowledge on nanovaccine design strategies and their potential to transition from laboratory development to clinical application.

articles.title: CEACAM5-Targeted Therapies in Solid Tumors: Biological Barriers and Next-Generation Precision Strategies
articles.summary: This review examines carcinoembryonic antigen-related cell adhesion molecule 5 (CEACAM5)-targeted therapies for solid tumors, focusing on the biological barriers that limit treatment efficacy and discussing emerging precision strategies to overcome these challenges.

articles.title: A Two-Stage Strategy to Reprogram Cyanine Photosensitizers as Controllable-Pyroptosis Inducers for Anticancer Phototherapy
articles.summary: Researchers developed a two-stage strategy to modify cyanine photosensitizers so they can trigger controlled pyroptosis (a form of programmed cell death) for anticancer phototherapy applications. This reprogramming approach enables more precise control over the photosensitizers' ability to induce cell death in cancer cells. The work represents a novel application of existing photosensitizer compounds for improved anticancer treatment outcomes.

articles.title: A defect-free nanofiber is not yet a medicine: The translational debt of pharmaceutical electrospinning
articles.summary: While pharmaceutical electrospinning enables production of sophisticated drug-loaded nanofiber architectures, achieving structural innovation does not automatically result in clinically or industrially viable medicines. The field faces a significant translational gap between laboratory development of defect-free nanofibers and the practical requirements for pharmaceutical products intended for clinical use and manufacturing scale-up.

articles.title: Skin barrier and beyond: From structural blueprint to rational skin-targeted therapeutics
articles.summary: This review examines the structural organization of the skin barrier and its implications for developing targeted therapeutic approaches. By understanding the skin barrier's fundamental architecture, researchers can design more effective skin-targeted drug delivery systems and treatments. The work bridges basic skin biology with practical strategies for rational pharmaceutical development in dermatology.
